predecessors.name: Ziyadid dynasty
predecessors.text: Zabid and the Tihama, where the last Ziyadid king died in 1018

successors.name: Mahdids
successors.text: Zabid and the Tihama, taken by Ali ibn Mahdi in 1158

ledger.x: 1022: Najah, an Abyssinian administrator, founds the Najahid emirate at Zabid.
1062: the Sulayhids take Zabid and the Tihama; Najah's children flee to Dahlak.
1067: the Najahids are back at Zabid and kill Ali al-Sulayhi on the pilgrimage road.
1087: Said al-Ahwal comes back to Zabid.
1089: the contest ends with the Najahids in Zabid.
1089 at the latest: the Najahids rule Zabid again.
1158: the Mahdids take Zabid and the Najahid dynasty ends.

wars.name: Sulayhid-Najahid wars
wars.outcome: The Sulayhids took Zabid in 1062; the Najahids killed Ali al-Sulayhi on the pilgrimage road (1066 or 1067) and were at Zabid again by 1067; al-Mukarram captured Zabid and Asma in 1082 and al-Ahwal fled to Dahlak; Said al-Ahwal returned in 1087 and was killed…

wars.name: Sulayhid-Zurayid siege of Zabid
wars.outcome: The Sulayhid leader al-Mufaddal besieged Zabid with the Zurayid brothers, who were killed in the siege; Zabid held.

wars.name: Mahdid conquest of Zabid
wars.outcome: Ali ibn Mahdi killed the last Najahid sovereign and the Mahdids took Zabid in 1158.

certainty.note: No boundary appears on any page; Zabid and the Tihama are named places.
